Tall
tôl
adj. (high in stature; rendering Hebrew rum and qomah)
Middle English tal, seemly, valiant; the sense of height came later. Scripture's tall people are the Anakims, and its tall trees are Sennacherib's boast.

Biblical Definition

Moses of the giants: the Emims were “a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims” (Deu 2:10), and the Zamzummims “a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; but the LORD destroyed them” (Deu 2:21). To Israel at Jordan: “A people great and tall, the children of the Anakims, whom thou knowest, and of whom thou hast heard say, Who can stand before the children of Anak!” (Deu 9:2). Sennacherib's boast: “I will cut down the tall cedar trees thereof, and the choice fir trees thereof” (2Ki 19:23; Isa 37:24).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines tall as high in stature; long and comparatively slender; applied to a person, or to a standing tree, mast, or pole.

expand to see more

TALL, a. High in stature; long and comparatively slender; applied to a person, or to a standing tree, mast or pole.

2. Sturdy; lusty; bold.

Key Scripture

Deu 9:2 — "A people great and tall, the children of the Anakims, whom thou knowest, and of whom thou hast heard say, Who can stand before the children of Anak!"

Deu 2:10 — "The Emims dwelt therein in times past, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims;"

Deu 2:21 — "A people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; but the LORD destroyed them before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead:"

2Ki 19:23 — "By thy messengers thou hast reproached the Lord, and hast said, With the multitude of my chariots I am come up to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Lebanon, and will cut down the tall cedar trees thereof, and the choice fir trees thereof: and I will enter into the lodgings of his borders, and into the forest of his Carmel."

Isa 37:24 — "By thy servants hast thou reproached the Lord, and hast said, By the multitude of my chariots am I come up to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Lebanon; and I will cut down the tall cedars thereof, and the choice fir trees thereof: and I will enter into the height of his border, and the forest of his Carmel."

Modern Corruption

The church counts the tall men on the other side, and Moses reminds Israel that the LORD had already destroyed two nations of them for other people.

expand to see more

Deuteronomy 9:2 quotes the proverb of the spies — Who can stand before the children of Anak! — and answers it in the next verse: the LORD thy God is he which goeth over before thee; as a consuming fire he shall destroy them. Moses had already told them in chapter 2 that God had done exactly this twice, for Moab and for Ammon, destroying peoples great and many and tall so that Lot's descendants could dwell in their place. The tall men had been cleared away for pagans; would He not clear them for His own? The fear of the tall is the fear that killed a generation at Kadesh, and it is the church's standing temptation — to measure the opposition and forget the record. Sennacherib's tall cedars are the boast from the other side, and Isaiah's answer to it was that the Assyrian had been a tool in a hand since before he was born.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew rum (H7311), to be high, tall; qomah (H6967), height, stature.

expand to see more

Hebrew ram (H7311) — high, tall; Deuteronomy 1:28, 2:10, 2:21, 9:2.

Hebrew qomah (H6967) — height, of the tall cedars; 2 Kings 19:23, Isaiah 37:24, 10:33.

Usage

"“Who can stand before the children of Anak!” — the spies' proverb, and the next verse."

"“A people great, and many, and tall… but the LORD destroyed them” — cleared away for Moab."

"“I will cut down the tall cedar trees thereof” — Sennacherib's boast."
